retention_is_manual: FOUNDER DECISION 13 Oct 2026 22:18 (R1 + Option A). Registrations are kept for at most 12 months and deleted sooner when no longer needed. Hosts.erase_after and the 'Erasure due' view only FLAG records; nothing in Airtable, the Worker or this schema deletes anything automatically, and no automation may be added to do so. Deletion is a human act in the weekly review: (1) delete the Hosts record; (2) delete its Consent proofs row and its Status log row, found by the identical timestamp the Worker writes to all three (Hosts.submitted_at = Consent proofs.given_at = Status log.at; the Status log row also carries record_ref = the Hosts record id); (3) add ONE anonymous row to 'Deletion log'. No email, email hash, name or record id survives a deletion. Airtable keeps deleted records in its trash for 7 days and in automatic base snapshots for the plan's snapshot period (Team plan, confirmed 13 Oct 2026: up to 1 year); PlotNua never restores deleted registration records. ARTISTS (14 Oct 2026): the same rule, the same 12-month maximum and the same human deletion, for the Artists table: delete the Artists record, then its Consent proofs and Status log rows (register = artist, identical timestamp: Artists.submitted_at = Consent proofs.given_at = Status log.at; the Status log row carries record_ref = the Artists record id), then add ONE anonymous Deletion log row with register = artist.
dates: Every date field: Date (ISO), include time, 24-hour, one fixed time zone for all collaborators. Created with Europe/Dublin, which is accepted: the Worker always sends UTC instants with a trailing Z, Airtable stores every dateTime as a UTC instant and returns UTC through the API, so the time zone setting changes only what a person sees. Formula results (erase_after, remove_after) should display in ISO date format (YYYY-MM-DD); they were created in US format (M/D/YYYY), which is a display-only change.
